prompt:
Create one finished opaque flat 16:9 landscape cultural-event poster for a neighbourhood rubber-block printing and shared reading evening for adults, displayed on a community centre digital screen. Approachable to first-time residents, energetic and mature. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Visual system: assertive constructed culture, flat cut ink-like planes with compact heavy straight-sided Korean grotesk typography, open humanist sans-serif practical information, attentive adult profiles. Citron ground, near-black text and hands, deep petrol structural planes, pale ivory reading paper. Crisp solid clean letter strokes. Controlled carved relief cuts appear only inside the nonletter print motif; no distress through letters, gradients, toy-like forms, tape or decorative ribbons.

Compose for the landscape, using a 720×405 proportional layout guide rather than a requested output resolution. The stable left 42% is a title/information spine. The right 53% is an active diagonal printing-to-reading paper field. At x28 y30, set the main Korean title in two word-group lines with the line break after its first word; approximately 49px type and 58px baseline step, contained in a 276×156 region. From x28 y210 downward, place the eight practical-information entries in their supplied order as eight clean horizontal rows, approximately 17px at this guide size, 21px row spacing, within 276×175. Preserve generous word spacing and open Hangul counters. Title and facts share one left alignment. First sight is title, then immediately date/time, venue, admission, fee, application, preparation, welcome down this single spine. At x323 y23 place the activity identification as one line of 19px medium sans. Keep all text fully in frame, with clear flat ground, and readable when the whole image is 720px wide.

Construct a substantial nonglyph scene occupying roughly x317–698 y57–386. Two adult upper-body profiles in the upper-right share one broad sheet: one person has a subtly open speaking mouth, both have visible eyes and gaze directed down toward the page. Heads about 65–80px at the guide scale. Both readers visibly support the same sheet at its clean edge, with fingers and hand ownership clear. A broad horizontal reader-facing part of that actual sheet holds the English entry, upright readable capitals around 23px, contained approximately x475 y176 in a 211×48 area; this line appears nowhere else. There is clear paper area around the line, free of hands or relief marks.

The SAME single sheet extends diagonally from the readers' held end toward the lower-right printing area, meeting a deep petrol table/plane. Make the continuity, full paper edge and diagonal motion plainly visible; it is a functional paper object, not a ribbon. A forearm enters from the lower right, fingers gripping the clean edge of a thick carved rubber slab and lifting one edge from the paper. Expose the inked underside at an angle, the slab's thickness, an air gap at the raised edge and the freshly transferred impression immediately beside/below it. Keep the complete slab and complete fresh impression visible, approximately 60–85px each. Use one specific asymmetric abstract nonletter motif, e.g. a stepped oval with an off-centre crescent cut and three short notch cuts. The exact same silhouette/cuts must visibly match on the inked rubber underside, the fresh adjacent paper impression and the reader-held end of the connected sheet. This repeated impression visibly connects making with shared reading. Maintain distinct boundaries for fingers, slab edge, rubber thickness, contact gap, impression and paper. Only nontext body/structural planes may leave the frame. Never crop eyes, mouths, gripping fingers, rubber thickness, full impression or English line.

Print only the following eleven literal entries, each exactly once. No labels or other text. Preserve every Hangul glyph, English capital, word space, number, middle dot, comma, colon and the en dash in the time range.
